t: 3229. Minimum Operations to Make Array Equal to Target
o: Each operation adds or subtracts 1 across a chosen subarray of nums; we want the minimum number of operations to transform nums into target. Only the difference array d[i] = target[i] - nums[i] matters. In example 1, d = [1,1,1,2] needs 2 operations (one covering the rise from 0 to 1, one covering the rise from 1 to 2). In example 2, d = [1,-2,2] needs 5.
k: Work on the difference array d; operations become +1/-1 range updates to make d all zero.
The minimum number of operations equals the total positive variation of d (with d treated as 0 outside the array): sum of max(0, d[i] - d[i-1]).
Positive and negative variation totals are equal when boundaries are 0, so counting rises suffices.

a.i: Think of d as a landscape that must be flattened to zero using ±1 rectangle removals. Each operation removes one unit of height across a contiguous interval, so the number of operations equals the total amount of 'rising edge' in the landscape, including the rise from the implicit 0 boundary at the left. Formally the answer is Σ max(0, d[i] - d[i-1]) with d[-1] = 0; falling edges are covered automatically because total rise equals total fall when both outer boundaries are zero.
s: Compute d[i] = target[i] - nums[i] on the fly.
For each i, add max(0, d[i] - prev) to the answer and set prev = d[i].

a.i: Repeatedly scan d, find maximal runs of positive values and decrement each by 1, and maximal runs of negative values and increment each by 1, counting one operation per run per round. This directly mimics performing the operations and terminates when d is all zero. It is easy to reason about but can be slow when entries are large (up to 1e8 rounds in the worst case), so it serves mainly as a correctness reference.
s: While any d[i] != 0: increment the operation counter.
In one sweep, for each maximal run of positive d values subtract 1 from the whole run; likewise add 1 to maximal negative runs.
Each run adjusted costs exactly one operation.
Return the counter when d is all zeros.
a.t: O(V · n) where V is the maximum absolute difference — potentially 1e13, so use only as intuition

w: Always present the O(n) variation formula in an interview; the simulation is only for building intuition. Use 64-bit answers (values up to 1e8 over 1e5 elements). Verify on the examples: [1,1,1,2] gives 2 and [1,-2,2] gives 5. Follow-up: what if operations were restricted to prefixes? Then the answer is simply the sum of positive differences from the boundary.
